comments.author: TallGuyShort
comments.story: Ask HN: What's the best technical talk you've heard?
comments.why: Interesting, accessible talk on Minix 3 architecture
comments.text: Andrew Tanenbaum presenting on Minix 3's architecture: [VIDEO] . Regardless of one's opinions on microkernels vs. monolithic kernels, it's a very interesting but accessible talk for those interested in lower-level systems and fault-tolerant architectures.

comments.author: shangxiao
comments.story: Hobby kernel and userspace, built mostly from scratch
comments.why: Suggested as a modular OS design direction
comments.text: Writing OS's is hard and there are no shortcuts. You should take a look at microkernels and the work Andrew Tanenbaum did with Minix 3 [1] and his modular design as this is the sort of direction you're probably looking for with customisable OS's. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: nickpsecurity
comments.story: Ask HN: Best practices for self-healing apps?
comments.why: One entry in a list of reliable-system examples
comments.text: Here's you some examples to learn from. Most are old enough that patents have expired: Why Do Computers Stop and What Can Be Done About It? (1985) [LINK] Their NonStop Architecture [LINK] QNX's systems are ultra-reliable, too [LINK] OpenVMS clusters' uptime was years to decades & mixed CPU ISA's [LINK] Systems that run forever and self-heal (Armstrong) [LINK] Microreboots [LINK] Minix 3: Microkernel-based, self-healing, POSIX OS [VIDEO]
